[P2] Clear buffering before closing the projection | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Codex plugin sends OpenClaw agent turns to Codex App Server and projects its results into session history and Gateway events. Awaiting the first attempt already runs `finalizeCodexAttempt()` and mirrors its terminal refusal. Refusals have `terminal.kind === "ok"`, so the mirror's deferred-failure exception does not apply. The retry gets another native turn ID and can publish a second terminal row for the same run; returning only its result cannot discard the first committed row. Stage terminal publication until escalation settles and verify one final outcome after history refresh. - [ ] **Read authorization failures from the canonical terminal result (P2)** - The prior blocker remains. `runCodexAppServerAttempt()` returns failures through `terminal`, not a top-level `promptError`. When Daybreak returns 401/403 before producing an assistant row, this reader reports `unavailable: false`, so the unavailable notice and cooloff record are skipped and subsequent refusals repeat the denied attempt. Consume the existing terminal projection and test an actual projector result without assistant output. - [ ] **Clear buffering before closing the projection (P2)** - The prior blocker remains. The added buffering state clears on assistant output or native completion, but local cancellation, timeout, or transport failure can reach `closeProjection()` without either event. This method immediately fences event emission, and UI run cleanup preserves the notice, leaving a finished run showing 'Cyber safety review'. End buffering before aborting the projection controller and cover closure without native completion. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Default-on escalation changes existing configurations from a terminal refusal to an additional model attempt; fresh-install and upgrade behavior, including disabled mode and denied entitlement, lacks registered-harness evidence. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The first refusal can own a terminal transcript row before the successful retry, leaving competing outcomes for one run after history refresh. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Canonical authorization failures can escape the denial cache, repeatedly incurring the provider reconnect ladder. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The PR body still describes removed session-window behavior and says the startup-budget raise is absent, although the pinned diff includes it. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Resolve the three retained findings, validate retry settlement and fresh/upgrade behavior through the registered harness, and update the stale implementation and budget claims in the PR body. ## Findings - [P1] Defer refusal transcript finalization until the retry decision — `extensions/codex/harness.ts:329-330` - [P2] Read authorization failures from the canonical terminal result — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/cyber-failover.ts:207-208` - [P2] Clear buffering before closing the projection — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts:94-95`
